release.description:
Orkasa is the CRM that real-estate agencies in Latin America run on: client files, property portfolio, viewings, offers and documents in one place.

This connector lets the broker ask about their own work, in their own words. «How is Mrs Herrera's file going?» returns the whole dossier — her operations and the stage each one is at, the property, the viewings, the offers, the documents and the latest messages — plus the next step Orkasa's Copilot recommends, and why. «What do I have today?» returns those steps in order: what is waiting on the agent first, and among those the most overdue. It also searches the portfolio by area, type, price and bedrooms, and reads the viewing schedule.

Four tools write: create a client, book a viewing, move an operation to the next stage, and record an offer. They respect the same locks as the app: an operation does not advance while its stage is still missing documents, and in that case the connector returns the list of what is missing instead of forcing the step. Publishing listings, generating mandates and sending documents for signature do not go through the connector.

The broker authorises specific permissions («see your leads», «book viewings»), sees which domain their data will be sent to before accepting, and can cut the access off from Settings › Connections. The assistant only sees what that user sees inside Orkasa: if they cannot see the rest of the office's clients in the app, they cannot see them here either.

Requires an Orkasa account attached to an agency.

release.description:
Find Japanese grants and public support programs using official data published by government agencies.

Rather than simply listing programs, this app compares public company information with program requirements and clearly separates confirmed matches, possible mismatches, missing information, and official sources. This helps users understand why a program may be relevant and what still needs to be verified.

The app can be used by business owners and project leaders researching support for their own organizations, as well as by professional advisors researching programs for their clients or preparing for consultations.

When useful, it can also reference public corporate information and historical selection statistics, and organize unresolved questions into a consultation brief for a qualified professional.

Results are provided for research and decision support only. They do not guarantee eligibility, selection, funding amounts, or legal compliance. Before applying, always confirm the latest official guidelines and information published by the administering organization.

Primary official sources
- J-Grants
- gBizINFO
- National Tax Agency Corporate Number System
- Financial Services Agency EDINET

Read what the dashboard draws: visitors over time, top pages, sources, countries, custom events, goal completions, funnel reports and who is on the site right now. Break the numbers down and filter them the same way the dashboard does.

It also sets sites up. Add a website and get its tracking snippet, create and edit goals and funnels, adjust tracking settings and site filters. It cannot alter or delete the analytics themselves, and there is no delete tool of any kind.

Sign in once through your browser. Nothing to paste, no key to create, no configuration beyond the server address. Statable collects no cookies, needs no analytics consent banner, and hosts the data in the EU.

release.description:
SuperBooks is bookkeeping for freelancers and small teams: bank transactions with AI categorisation, invoices, customers, a receipt inbox and document vault, a time tracker, and financial reports. The SuperBooks plugin lets ChatGPT work your books from your own account: list and inspect transactions, fix a category or workflow status, find unpaid or overdue invoices, draft a new invoice for a customer (drafts are never sent until you say so), look up customers and add new ones, search receipts and documents, match a receipt to a transaction, start and stop time tracking, and pull profit & loss, burn rate, runway, spending by category, revenue, balances, top customers and recurring expenses.

Access runs through OAuth 2.1 with PKCE and dynamic client registration; you approve read and write scopes on the consent screen, and a tool whose scope you did not grant is never offered. Destructive operations — deleting transactions, customers, categories, tags, documents or inbox items, and voiding invoices — are hidden behind a team-level "Destructive AI tools" switch that is OFF by default, on top of the credential's own scope. Every credential is rate-limited (120 calls a minute) and can be revoked at any time from Settings → Developer.

The plugin never moves money: bank connections, payments and billing are only reachable in the app. Sending an invoice e-mails it to your customer, and nothing else leaves your account. No purchases are made in-tool, no images, video or audio are generated, and no ads are served.

release.description: ZeniFlow is a personal finance app for tracking money across wallets. release.description:
Chashmalink answers questions about Israeli household electricity from measured smart-meter data rather than estimates off a bill.

Behind it sits an analysed corpus of more than 20,000 Israeli households across 500+ municipalities, each a full hourly export from Israel Electric Corporation — up to 17,520 meter readings per home. That is what lets these tools answer with a number rather than a rule of thumb.

Ten read-only tools:

• compare_electricity_plans — rank every plan on the Israeli market by what it would save a specific household, per month and per year. Takes a monthly kWh figure or, far better, a 24-hour load curve.

• simulate_solar_tracks — price Israel's two mutually exclusive rooftop solar tracks against a real load shape, with payback and a recommendation. Which one pays more depends on WHEN a household consumes — the thing a roof-area calculator cannot see.

• get_city_consumption_benchmark — median monthly consumption, profile mix and 24-hour curve for a given Israeli city.

• get_national_load_curve — national demand by hour, day of week and season.

• classify_consumption_profile — classify a home as evening, night, morning, weekend or balanced, with peakiness and a night-shift opportunity figure.

• estimate_appliance_cost, size_air_conditioner, compare_ev_running_cost — running costs for appliances, air conditioning and electric cars at the current tariff.

• get_supplier_directory — every supplier and plan with its discount structure.

• how_to_export_my_iec_data — how a household downloads its own consumption file.

Privacy: no per-household data is reachable here. Every figure is either computed from the caller's own inputs or is a population aggregate published only where at least 25 analysed households sit behind it; a thinner cohort is refused rather than answered thinly. Nothing here writes, submits or contacts anyone.

Free, no account, no API key. Figures are in shekels and kWh.

release.description:
Stratify backtests Indian index option strategies on a year of real 1-minute NIFTY options data. Describe the trade in plain words — the legs, when to enter, how to manage it while it is open — and the server runs it against every trading day in the window and returns what actually happened.

Every result carries P&L after real charges (brokerage, STT, exchange and SEBI fees, GST, stamp duty) and modelled slippage, return on margin from a SPAN calibration, and an honesty panel: an out-of-sample split, walk-forward folds, a bootstrap interval, and a deflated Sharpe that accounts for how many variants you have already tried. No ratio is reported below 30 trades. Every backtest gets a shareable report page with the equity curve, the rules card and every trade.

The open strategy protocol covers any number of legs on any expiry; strikes by delta, premium, points or percent; per-leg stops and targets; rolling a tested side; entry gates on VIX, index RSI/EMA/SMA and combined premium; clock-time entries and exits; and portfolio rules such as pausing after consecutive losses.

Data never leaves the server — a backtest returns results, not rows. No trades are executed and no financial advice is given: the service never calls a strategy good. Free tier: NIFTY, one year, 100 backtests an hour. Requires a free Stratify account (sign in via OAuth).

Bucket CRM is the CRM equipment dealers use to sell and service machines: pressure washers, floor scrubbers, compressors and the parts, chemicals and service contracts that go with them. This plugin gives ChatGPT a window into your dealership's customers and tasks, under your own login.

Everything runs as you. ChatGPT sees exactly what you can see in Bucket CRM and can change only what you are allowed to change. Changes that overwrite existing information ask you to confirm first. There is no way to delete anything through the plugin.

Organize web pages recommended by ChatGPT into a tab tree you can open in Keep Browser and share with others using a single link. Preserve groups, parent–child relationships, and tab order. A summary page is included as the first tab, showing page names and brief descriptions.

First ask ChatGPT to organize the content and URLs in your chat. Review them, then send a separate message asking to share them with Keep Browser. Open the share link returned in the chat and select “Open in Keep Browser” on the sharing page to import the tab tree into the Keep Browser app. Send the same share link to someone else so they can import the same tree.

Try it in two steps:
1. Ask ChatGPT: “Plan a day in Waikiki with three lunch options and two nearby sights, including reasons and official links.”
2. Review the recommendations, then send a separate message: “Share this with Keep Browser.”

Anyone with the share link or summary URL can view the shared content and included descriptions. Do not include personal information or private links.

Share links expire 30 days after creation or the most recent import, whichever is later. Viewing a page does not extend this period. The summary page also becomes unavailable when the share expires or is deleted.

Importing requires the Keep Browser app for Android or iOS.

release.description:
Pile Capacity estimates the axial bearing and uplift capacity of cast-in-situ bored piles and CFA piles from a soil profile and a pile schedule, and solves the inverse problem: the length each pile needs to carry a stated compression and tension load.

Describe the ground and the piles in plain language, such as layer thicknesses and types, undrained shear strength or friction angle, rock UCS, groundwater level, pile diameters, target loads and factors of safety. The connector resolves that into a complete analysis input and shows you the resolved input, every assumption it had to make for a value you did not give, and the provenance of each field (your value, an engineering convention, or a default), so you confirm or correct the design before anything is calculated.

Confirmed designs return one summary per pile: required length, toe level, allowable and ultimate compression and uplift capacity, and the factors used. You can then render the full calculation report as a PDF with charts, formulas and per-layer tables, or as an Excel workbook with live formulas, and save the design into a project in your Pile Capacity account, where it opens in the web app like any other design.

SI and US customary units are both supported. The connector picks the system from the units you write and warns you when your words and your numbers disagree.

Requires a hetGE account with an active Pile Capacity licence. Sign-in is OAuth against id.hetge.com; the connector never sees your password and reads only the design inputs your assistant sends, plus at most one sentence of your wording when it contains unit words, used only to check the units.

release.description:
Rightis is a public registry of identity rights. People and rights holders
register their face, voice and persona, and set which AI uses they allow,
which need their approval, and which they refuse.

This plugin lets ChatGPT check that registry before generating a likeness,
a voice or a persona of a real person. Ask about someone by name or by their
Rights ID and you get back what they allow, what needs approval, and whether
they have refused use of their data for AI training.

It is read-only and needs no account or key. It never returns photos,
recordings or contact details. Someone who is not registered is unconfirmed,
which is not the same as cleared for use.

release.description:
HouseLoop is a Kansas City real-estate brokerage and search site. HouseLoop gives ChatGPT read-only access to HouseLoop's live Heartland MLS data for the Kansas City metro (Kansas and Missouri) through six tools.

Search active and coming-soon homes by city, county, ZIP, school district, price, beds, baths, square footage and property type — and by features HouseLoop reads from each listing's photos with its own image classifier, which is how it finds homes on details the MLS record never captures: white kitchen cabinets, a frameless glass shower, a stamped concrete patio. Ask list_home_features for the ids and value facets the search accepts; a feature id it does not recognise is an error naming what it does accept, never a silently wider search.

Then get one home's numbers (price, $/sqft, tax, HOA, list date, days on market, status), HouseLoop's written buyer FAQ for that home, sell-through market statistics for a city, ZIP or county, and HouseLoop's own value estimate and range for an address.

Every result names its source, carries the MLS GRID attribution required by the data licence, and includes an absolute houseloop.ai URL to cite. Search results report the total number of matching homes alongside the page actually returned, so a count is never mistaken for the whole answer.

Read-only. No account, no sign-in, no personal data. Kansas City metro only.

release.description:
FinalPeace helps families write a will, power of attorney and healthcare directive, and keep them in one place. This plugin gives ChatGPT three tools anyone can use without an account.

State document requirements. For any of the 50 states, it looks up what it takes to sign a will, a financial power of attorney, a health care proxy or a living will: how many witnesses, whether a notary is needed, who can't serve as a witness, and whether the state publishes an official form. Every answer shows the date it was last checked and the source it was checked against.

After-a-loss checklist. The practical list of what needs doing after someone dies, grouped by when it matters: the first 24 to 48 hours, the first week, the first month, and ongoing.

Planning check. Tell it what you already have, such as a will, a healthcare agent or a power of attorney, and it ranks what's missing by what would go wrong without it. Anything you haven't answered comes back as a question.

If you already have a FinalPeace account, a fourth tool explains how to connect it.

FinalPeace is not a law firm and doesn't give legal advice. State rules change, so check the date on each answer and confirm anything important with your state or a lawyer.

release.description:
Foodzilla is the nutrition platform dietitians, nutritionists and health coaches use to plan, track and run their practice. This plugin puts that work in the conversation.

Ask ChatGPT for a recipe and it is written, costed for macros and saved to your library. Ask for a week of meals to a calorie and macro target and you get a template ready to review and assign. Add a food to your own database from a label or a link. Draft an intake form, set your booking hours, publish a post to your clients, or check where your subscription stands.

Your clients can connect too, if you let them. A client asks their own assistant to log a meal, water, a workout, their sleep or their weight, and to read the plan for the day. Everything they log lands in their diary, where their coach already looks.

Your client data is not reachable from your connection. A coach connection cannot see a client list, a client's diary, their notes or their record, and it cannot message anyone. It works on the coach's own material only: recipes, foods, meal plan templates, collections, forms, booking hours, content, the store and the subscription. A client connection reaches that one client's own record and nobody else's, and cannot change the plan or the targets their coach set for them. Names and email addresses never go into our server logs.

You need a Foodzilla account. Foodzilla Autopilot is included with the Professional plan and above. Client access is a switch the coach controls, for one client or for everyone.

release.description:
Intuizi connects ChatGPT to the Intuizi data platform, where marketing teams turn de-identified signal data into audiences and deliver them to their marketing destinations. The plugin queries the Large Behavioral Model, Intuizi's flagship LQM, trained on de-identified, real-world behavioral signal. Responses include counts, statuses, and metadata. Audience data never enters the chat and is sent only to destinations configured in the Intuizi console.

What you can do:
- Look up reference catalogs: POI categories and brands, apps, web domains, CTV channels, Transactions merchants, demographic and profile attributes, countries, and signal providers.
- Estimate how large an audience would be before you build it, then create audiences from POI visits, app usage, web domains, CTV viewing, Transactions, demographics, profile attributes, home location, or your own cohorts, alone or combined with AND, OR, and NOT IN.
- Grow a completed audience with a lookalike model and follow the model run.
- Preview a frequency range, then activate the audience to a delivery destination your team has already set up in the Intuizi console.
- Create cohorts from your own files or from an existing audience, and manage projects, POI categories, brands, and location submissions.
- Check your organization's data-scan usage against its limits.

Every tool wraps a documented Intuizi API v2 endpoint, so validation, permissions, and rate limits match the API exactly. Read-only tools are marked read-only and delete tools are marked destructive. You need an Intuizi console account: connect with one-click OAuth, approve access in your browser, and the plugin sees only the projects and data your account can see.

release.description:
Klap turns long videos into short vertical clips for TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts, right from ChatGPT.

Share a YouTube, Twitch, Kick or Vimeo link, or any public video URL, and ask for shorts. Klap finds the most engaging moments, reframes them to 9:16 around the speaker, adds animated captions and ranks every clip by virality score. Clipping runs in the background: a live card shows its progress, then turns into a gallery of shorts you can play right in the conversation.

From the gallery you can:
• Watch each short with its captions
• Download a short as an MP4
• Schedule a short to your connected YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, LinkedIn or Facebook accounts, at the time you choose
• Open a short in the Klap editor to fine-tune captions, layout and length

You can also guide the clipping ("the funniest moments about pricing", "15-second clips", "5 clips at most"), set the spoken language, and ask for your recent projects.

Using Klap in ChatGPT requires a Klap account. Exports and scheduling follow your Klap plan. Social accounts are connected on klap.app, and ChatGPT never receives their credentials. Klap only publishes a post after you confirm the short, the accounts, the time and the caption.

Sign in with a 3DPACK.ING account to use it. A free account includes a monthly allowance of packs.

release.description:
Biohacking Kompakt ist eine deutschsprachige Faktencheck-Datenbank zu Supplements, Peptiden, Therapien und Longevity-Themen. Zu jedem Thema gibt es den BK-Score: fünf Achsen, die den Wissensstand beschreiben – wie gut am Menschen untersucht, wie gut die Sicherheitslage untersucht ist, wie lange und breit angewendet, wie plausibel der Mechanismus und wie groß der Hype. Dazu die Richtung, in die die vorhandene Evidenz zeigt, und die passende Folge des Podcasts „Biohacking Kompakt“.

Der Score bewertet den Wissensstand, nicht die Substanz. Die App liest live von biohackingkompakt.de, verkauft nichts und gibt keine medizinische Beratung. Zu verschreibungspflichtigen und nicht zugelassenen Substanzen liefert sie ausschließlich die Einordnung der Studienlage – ohne Dosierung, ohne Anwendung, ohne Bezugsquelle.

Paste a listing’s Registration details—region of issuance, licence type and licence number—or provide a registered business name, address or government management number. release.description:
League & Tournament Scheduler builds game schedules for youth and adult sports leagues and tournaments. Describe your season in plain words: the dates, your fields and when they're open, your divisions and teams, and any limits, like a team that can't play Tuesdays or two teams that share a coach.

It reads every rule back to you first, so a misunderstanding gets caught before any games are placed. Then it builds the schedule and hands it to a separate checker that tests every game against every rule. A schedule is only shown as final when the checker confirms it. If the rules can't all fit, such as more games than open field times, it names the rules that collide and suggests what to change.

What it handles:
• Round robins where each pair meets 1 to 4 times
• Pool play followed by a single-elimination bracket, or a straight bracket with byes
• Several divisions sharing the same fields
• Weekly field times, tournament dates, holidays, and field closures
• Team blackout dates and days, earliest and latest start times, and shared coaches
• Games per day and per week, rest days, and time between games
• Balanced home and away games and fair early and late slots
• Mid-season changes that keep played games where they were

When you're ready to share, it publishes a link with a printable schedule, a spreadsheet download, and a calendar feed for each team.

No account or sign-in needed. Made by Red Finch Publishing LLC.

release.description: Noon is an AI recruiter. Source candidates for a role, review who Noon found, edit the outreach it sends, and diagnose how a role's search is going.

interface.short_description: AI sourcing and outreach
interface.long_description:
Noon is an AI recruiter. Connect it to ChatGPT to source candidates for a job, review who Noon found, shape the outreach Noon sends, and find out why a role's search is or isn't working, all from a conversation.

What you can do
• Source candidates: describe a role or paste a job description, and Noon creates the role and starts searching for matching people.
• Review the feed: see the candidates Noon surfaced for a role, with its reasoning for each match.
• Accept or reject candidates: accepting adds someone to the role's project (and starts outreach when auto-contact is on); rejecting with a reason teaches Noon what to avoid.
• Give feedback on the feed as a whole ("too many consultants", "more fintech backgrounds"): Noon re-scores the current candidates and adjusts future sourcing.
• Read and rewrite outreach sequences: LinkedIn invites, InMails, emails and follow-ups.
• Diagnose a role's search: funnel counts, top rejection reasons, which single requirement is blocking otherwise-qualified people, and what loosening each filter would add.
• Look up a candidate's profile and the evaluation behind Noon's decision.

Who it's for
Recruiters, sourcers and hiring managers who use Noon.

Requirements and limits
• You need a Noon account (www.noon.ai). You sign in with your Noon login when you connect, and ChatGPT only sees the roles and candidates in your Noon workspace.
• Outreach goes out from the email and LinkedIn accounts connected in your Noon portal.
• Noon can't delete roles, change billing, or access other companies' workspaces from ChatGPT.
• Everything done here also shows up in your Noon portal.
interface.default_prompt: List my open Noon roles and show the newest candidates for the most recent one.
default_prompts: List my open Noon roles and show the newest candidates for the most recent one.
Source senior backend engineers in New York with 5+ years of Python.

release.description: Parametric CAD for 3D printing, by chat: design and edit 3D parts, explore them in a live 3D viewer, then download STL, STEP or 3MF files from PartForge.

interface.short_description: Parametric CAD by chat
interface.long_description:
PartForge is parametric CAD for 3D printing that you drive by chatting. Ask ChatGPT for a 3D-printable part, such as a bracket, a cable clip, a phone stand, an enclosure or a replacement knob, and it writes the part as parametric CAD code in your PartForge account, builds the 3D model, and checks it before telling you it's done.

The part opens in PartForge's live 3D viewer right in the chat. Orbit it, adjust its dimensions with the sliders, and press Keep Settings to save the values you like. Open it in PartForge to download an STL or 3MF for your 3D printer and slicer, or a STEP file for other CAD software.

Every model is parametric: change a length, a wall thickness or a hole size and the whole part updates, so one design fits the screw, the shelf or the printer you actually have. ChatGPT can render the part from any angle, check details that matter for printing, such as wall thickness and whether it fits the print bed, read PartForge's documentation, and build on designs from the public PartForge library of 3D-printable parts.

When you're happy, ChatGPT can publish the part with a name and description, or make it private again. PartForge never sees your conversation, only the requests ChatGPT makes to your account.

release.description: Save job postings to JobHawk and keep track of your applications, interviews, and follow-ups.

interface.short_description: Track your job applications
interface.long_description:
JobHawk keeps track of your job search while you talk it through. When you find a posting worth keeping, ask the assistant to save it. It goes into your JobHawk tracker with the job title, company, and link, plus the location, salary range, and posting text when you share them.

From the same chat you can ask what you've applied to and see your applications grouped by status. When something changes, ask the assistant to move an application to its new status, for example from applied to interview. You can add a note to any saved application, like a recruiter's name or what they said about timing. Each note is stamped with the date and never replaces the ones before it. You can also ask what's coming up and see your scheduled interviews and follow-ups for the next week, or up to a month ahead if you ask.

JobHawk is for people in an active job search who have more open applications than they want to keep in their head.

A few limits to know about. JobHawk saves what the assistant passes along from your message. It doesn't open or read the posting page, so if you share only a link, the assistant will ask you for the job title and company. It can't delete applications, apply to jobs for you, or search job listings. Interviews and follow-up reminders are added in the JobHawk web app. In the chat you can see them but not create them.

You need a JobHawk account to save anything. Until you connect one, a save shows you a preview and stores nothing. Connecting opens a JobHawk sign-in page, where you can sign in or create an account. Everything you save here also shows up in JobHawk on the web.

default_prompts: Help me keep track of a job I just applied to

release.description: Keep track of a vegetable garden: what is growing where, everything done to it, and what to sow, harvest and water next, timed for where the garden is.

interface.short_description: When to sow, where you garden
interface.long_description:
Gardener's Almanac keeps track of a vegetable garden: what is growing where, everything done to it, and what comes next. Connected to ChatGPT, the garden can be worked by describing it. Say the beds were watered before breakfast and it goes in the log; ask what needs doing this week and the to-do list comes back; ask whether tomorrow is worth watering and ChatGPT checks the same forecast the app does.

Sowing, planting and watering times are worked out for your own ground. You say where the garden is, once, and the timing comes from that place's own climate, anywhere in the world. Every plant is stored as numbers: the warmth a seed needs to germinate, the days from sowing to a first picking, the cold it will and will not take. The same plant gives the right answer in Palermo and in Luleå.

Each growing area keeps its own soil moisture estimate, fed by the forecast where the garden is. Pots dry in hours where open ground takes days, and a greenhouse never waters itself.

Sowing, planting out, watering, weeding, harvests and notes are kept as a permanent record that spans years. It answers "when did the garlic go in last year?", and it is what makes next season's advice better than this season's.

A garden can be shared with a writer, who can log, plan and edit, or a reader, who sees everything and changes nothing. ChatGPT acts as you, with your role in each garden, and can do nothing you couldn't do yourself in the app.

Signing in is by a code sent to your email address, and a new address creates an account.

No ads, no advertising profiles, no third-party analytics. Made by one person in Sweden, on servers in the EU.
capabilities: See what needs doing this week
Find plants and add them to a bed

interface.long_description:
Manage your AI receptionist, AI website assistant, and AI front desk from ChatGPT. InsertChat assistants answer customers across website chat, phone, WhatsApp, email, and SMS, using your business knowledge. Your team handles follow-ups in one shared inbox.

Use InsertChat in ChatGPT to:
- Get a front desk brief across your accessible assistants, with urgent, unassigned, waiting, and needs-you queues.
- Review receptionist calls and website conversations, summarize requests, and prepare callback briefs or reply drafts.
- Find leads and customer contacts, read their submitted inquiries, and look up related conversations.
- Check website-assistant knowledge and training, identify questions from customer conversations, and add a selected FAQ or business page.
- Review monthly conversation, resolution, contact, satisfaction, and credit reports.
- Open your workspace beside ChatGPT. Supported hosts also offer view navigation, reply-box drafts, composer mentions, and start-page/default-assistant settings.

Includes guided workflows for AI receptionist reviews, website-assistant knowledge, and front desk handovers.

An InsertChat account and connected workspace are required. Contacts require an owner or admin; reports also require analytics access. ChatGPT prepares drafts for you to review and send. Calling customers, booking appointments, publishing assistants, and changing phone routing are done through your configured InsertChat workflows, not these tools. Adding a URL imports one page, uses one credit and one source slot, and does not crawl the website. Setup and training checks do not verify every channel or prove a phone line or website widget is live. App view controls depend on host support; otherwise use result cards and drafts in chat.

release.description: Connect OpenAI to Orgvue for workforce data analysis and organizational modeling in the US region.

interface.short_description: Explore Orgvue workforce data
interface.long_description:
Orgvue is the organizational design and workforce planning platform used by enterprises to model, cost and reshape their organizations. Connect OpenAI to Orgvue to explore workforce data, organizational structures, and planning scenarios.

In plain, natural language, ask questions about your workforce data: spans and layers, headcount by function, cost of a proposed structure, the gap between your current and future-state organization, or anything else you might want to know.

Ask workforce modelling questions and see the changes happening directly in Orgvue. You’ll get trusted answers grounded in your Orgvue data. See the impact of a scenario before you commit, draft the narrative for a restructure paper, or quickly pull the numbers you need for a board meeting.

Access follows your existing Orgvue permissions. OpenAI sees only the workspaces and datasets you're already entitled to, and only when you ask.

Orgvue remains the trusted source of workforce data and organizational scenarios, while OpenAI provides a conversational way to interact with them.

What you can do:
- Query datasets and properties across your Orgvue workspaces
- Summarize org structures - reporting lines, spans, layers, vacancies
- Ask the agent workforce modelling questions and instantly visualise the impact of changes in Orgvue
- Pull metrics and aggregations for reports, papers and presentations
- Explain what a dataset contains before you dig into it

release.description: Paste a Solidity or Anchor contract and get an instant security scan — reentrancy, access control, signer checks, unchecked math — with line numbers, severity and a fix for each finding.

interface.short_description: Scan Solidity & Anchor code
interface.long_description:
Heuristic security scan of Solidity and Solana (Anchor / native Rust) contracts: reentrancy patterns, missing access control, tx.origin, delegatecall, weak randomness, unchecked calls, missing signer / owner / PDA bump checks, unchecked arithmetic and more — each with line numbers, severity and a fix, plus an overall letter grade. Read-only: the code you paste is analysed in memory and never stored.

Tools:
• quick_audit — Static heuristic scan of a Solidity or Solana (Anchor / Rust) contract: findings with severity, line numbers and fixes, plus a letter grade.

Targets questions like: “audit my solidity contract”; “smart contract security checker”; “is this contract safe”; “solidity vulnerability scanner”; “anchor program audit”; “reentrancy check”.

Documentation: https://tokenos.ai/mcp/contract-audit

Outputs are informational — on-chain reads, deterministic calculators and heuristic scans — not financial, legal or security advice. TokenOS is non-custodial and never holds keys or funds; anything you launch, deploy or sign happens from your own wallet.
capabilities: Heuristic security scan for Solana Anchor / Rust

release.description: Read-only access to a consumer brand's sell-out analytics in Ciro: sales, stock, out-of-stocks, purchase suggestions, saved dashboards and data freshness across retail chains.

interface.short_description: Sell-out and stock analytics
interface.long_description:
Ciro is a sell-out analytics platform for consumer brands that sell through retail chains. It brings together the sales and stock data each chain shares with its suppliers, links the chain's product and store codes to the brand's own catalog, and keeps that data current.

Ciro for ChatGPT answers questions with that data for the Ciro organization you connect:
- Sales and units by retail chain, banner, brand, category, product, store, region or time, including comparisons with last year or last month.
- Stock, out-of-stocks and stock coverage by product and store.
- Purchase suggestions to reach your target days of inventory.
- Your saved Ciro dashboards, over their own date range or another one.
- Data freshness: the last day with sales and the last stock report for each chain, and the state of each integration.

It's read-only: it can't change data, settings or users in Ciro. You approve each connection for one Ciro organization, and your access is checked again on every request.

Ciro is built for key account managers, sales teams and demand planners at consumer brands, mainly in Latin America. You need a Ciro account with access to an organization. Answers reflect the retail chains your organization has connected, and data usually arrives one day late.

interface.short_description: Email templates & automations
interface.long_description:
Send & Retain is an email automation service. It creates, sends and tracks a company's transactional and marketing email — order confirmations, welcome emails, abandoned-cart reminders, win-back campaigns — and this plugin lets you run all of it from a conversation: the templates, the automations that send them, the contacts they go to, and the sending setup behind them.

Stand up a company's programme from its business type: a brand kit, starter templates and the matching automations (welcome, abandoned cart, order updates, win-back), created paused. Write and revise react.email templates in the company's own brand and voice, render them with sample data, and publish when they are right. Design event-triggered automations with delays, send windows, branches and A/B variants, preview every email in an automation, and check what would block it before it goes live. Manage contacts, attributes and segments, read delivery and engagement metrics by template and by day, search the message log, and triage bounces and complaints.

Built for founders, marketers and agencies running email for one company or a portfolio of them.

Safety by design: there is no bulk send. Every message has one recipient, and mail reaches many people only through an automation a person explicitly enabled. Automations are always created paused, and enabling one is a separate, confirmed step. Each company has a send kill switch and an optional daily cap. Bounces and complaints suppress addresses automatically, and complaint suppressions can never be removed. Provider API keys are entered only on the Send & Retain settings page, never in chat.

Limitations: email only (no SMS, push or social posting). Sending needs a connected provider or platform sending and a verified domain, which a person sets up once per company. Connecting requires a Send & Retain account.

release.description: Brain Rot Index, Focus Room and a 7-day plan to use your phone less.

interface.short_description: Check your brain rot level
interface.long_description:
Nobrainrot shows you how much of your life your phone is taking, then helps you take it back.

The Brain Rot Index is a 2-minute self-check: two sliders (daily phone hours and age) and 10 questions adapted from the Smartphone Addiction Scale – Short Version (Kwon et al., 2013). You get a score out of 100, one of eight habit types (like Night Scroller or Phantom Checker), and an estimate of the years you would spend on a screen before 80 at your current rate. You can share your result with a link.

Then do something about it:
• Focus Room: name the task, pick 25, 45 or 90 minutes, put the phone away. A live timer runs in the chat and you get a short receipt at the end.
• 7-day detox plan: one offline action a day, built around your habit type or what you want to fix (nights, work, social media).
• Screen time receipt: share your daily screen time and see what it adds up to per week, per year and per decade.
• Shift: a physical NFC puck you tap with your iPhone to lock distracting apps. Works with the Shift app for iOS.

No account, no email. We store your score, type, hours and age so your share link works, never your name. A self-check, not a medical diagnosis.

release.description: App Store Optimization for your own iOS and Android apps: keyword research, rank tracking, ASO score, competitor keywords and review replies from your ASOScan account.

interface.short_description: App Store ranking and keywords
interface.long_description:
ASOScan is an ASO skill and plugin for ChatGPT: App Store Optimization (ASO) software for iOS and Android apps, built and run by one app developer. Use ASO with ChatGPT: connect your ASOScan account and ask about your own apps in plain words.

What it does:
- App store ranking and Google Play store ASO. ASOScan reads your ASO score and its recommendations and tells you what to fix first, like an app store optimization checklist for your own listing.
- App keywords. App store keyword research with search volume and difficulty, keyword opportunities you could rank for, and tracking for the ones you pick.
- App store rank tracker. See where you rank for each tracked keyword and how the rank moved day by day, so you can see why your app is not showing in search.
- App store category ranking. See your app's chart position in its category over time.
- ASO audit. Check your app title and subtitle, keywords and description, see what changed over time, and draft listing text for other languages.
- App competitor analysis. Add a competitor by its store link and see the keywords it ranks for, its category rank and its rating history.
- App review analysis. See sentiment, top topics, bugs and feature requests, and get AI drafts of review replies. A reply goes to the store only after you approve the exact text, and only for apps connected to App Store Connect or Google Play Console.

Why teams use it: one set of app store optimization tools for the whole ASO job on both stores, with your real numbers right in the chat. Good ASO improves organic rankings, and ASOScan helps you rank better. It does not promise a rank.

What it does not do: it does not publish listing text to the stores, and it has no download or revenue data. Drafts stay in your ASOScan account.

You need an ASOScan account to see your own numbers. Without an account, the built-in skills still answer general ASO questions.

release.description: Cited briefings on the Iran–US war from World War Watcher: daily dispatches, a dated event timeline, a graded source registry, an escalation score, US oil supply, Gulf cloud and submarine-cable status, and curated weapon stockpiles.

interface.short_description: Cited Iran–US war briefings
interface.long_description:
World War Watcher tracks the Iran–US war and its effects on shipping, energy, cloud infrastructure and connectivity. Ask what happened on a given day or over a period, what a source reported and how credible it is, how intense the war is now and how that has changed, where US crude and the Strategic Petroleum Reserve stand, whether Gulf cloud regions and Red Sea and Hormuz cables are affected, or how many interceptors and missiles each side holds.

Every answer comes from World War Watcher's human-curated record: daily dispatches, a dated timeline of over 1,400 events with their sources, a registry of graded sources, and live feeds. Each result carries a link to the page it came from, so claims can be checked.

Limitations: it covers the Iran–US war only; it reads public data and changes nothing; the escalation score measures current intensity and is not a forecast; stockpile counts are curated estimates with a confidence grade and an assessment date; it gives no trading advice and does not predict strikes. Data is licensed CC BY-NC 4.0.

interface.short_description: Pressure-test startup ideas

GoNoGo validates startup and business ideas: a live voice interview with an AI startup mentor, market research, and a GO or NO-GO verdict on whether the idea is worth building.

Ask ChatGPT to pressure-test your idea and Alex, GoNoGo's AI startup mentor, appears right in the chat as a live talking video. Press Start and talk to him out loud. - See your GoNoGo projects and whether their research is still running

GoNoGo works with your GoNoGo account: you connect it once, and your interviews and projects are saved there. Your voice is used only to run the conversation and is not recorded.

release.description: Qualified human outcomes at the AI boundary: attorney review of SaaS launch legal pages, and on-site tasks in the US.

interface.short_description: Human sign-off for your AI
interface.long_description:
HumanFn is the escalation layer AI agents call when software alone shouldn't finish the task. It provides bounded, human-produced outcomes (Human Functions) with a defined scope, deliverable, turnaround and qualification. They're outcomes, not a marketplace: there are no profiles to browse or people to hire, and the user always decides whether to go ahead.

SaaS Launch Legal Review: a licensed attorney reviews a SaaS's final Terms of Service and Privacy Policy before launch and returns material issues, recommended revisions and answers to up to 3 founder questions, with a target turnaround of 2 business days. When launch-ready legal pages haven't been reviewed by an attorney, check_saas_legal_review (read-only) assesses fit and timing and shows the service's scope and terms. It is skipped for legal education, placeholder text and early ideas. HumanFn is still validating this service: accepting it records the user's interest, fulfillment isn't guaranteed yet, and the app says so before the user decides. HumanFn is not a law firm and does not give legal advice; using the app creates no attorney-client relationship.

On-site physical tasks: a local person goes to an address to check, photograph, measure, verify, wait for or pick up something, and returns structured proof. A person reviews each request first, and nothing is arranged until the user approves it on HumanFn's own site. Phoenix, Arizona metro fully supported; elsewhere in the US best effort; outside the US declined.

Anything else that needs a qualified human: find_human_function. Needs HumanFn doesn't cover yet are recorded to shape future services.

No account or sign-in needed.

release.description: Create a website with AI from a brief, then keep editing it in your own UiChemy account and pull it into WordPress.

interface.short_description: Create WordPress sites with AI
interface.long_description:
UiChemy lets you create a website with AI by chatting. Build and edit WordPress-ready sites without starting from a blank page. Describe a business or paste a client brief, and we draft a multi-page site from the UiChemy section library: sitemap, layouts, copy, colours and fonts. The result is a real project in your own UiChemy account that you keep editing on the UiChemy canvas.

What you can do:
- Build a new multi-page site from a brief, with layouts chosen from the UiChemy library and copy written to fit each slot.
- Edit an existing project: palette, fonts, buttons, cards, spacing, headings, body copy, logo, sections and pages.
- Import a site you already have (HTML, CSS and JS, or a zip) into a UiChemy project.
- Run responsive and validation checks before you hand a site over.
- Mark a finished project as exported so the UiChemy WordPress plugin can pull it into Elementor or Gutenberg.

Who it is for: freelancers, agencies and site owners who build on WordPress.

Good to know:
- You sign in with your own UiChemy account. This app only reaches projects in the account you connect, and some accounts need access to creation features before the tools work.
- We ask for your confirmation before anything that deletes a page, section, post or project, and before publishing or unpublishing a site.
- You can publish a finished project as a live site on a UiChemy address, check its status, list your sites and take one offline. It does not connect your own domain, change your hosting or log in to your WordPress site. You can also pull the project into WordPress with the UiChemy WordPress plugin.
- Use your own content and images, or content you have the right to use.

Planning a trip? Ask what a route would cost, for example Teterboro to Miami. BEACON works out the flight time from the owner's own numbers and gives an approximate total, including positioning from where the aircraft is parked when the owner charges for it. Ready to go ahead? BEACON can send your trip request, or a buyer's inquiry, straight to the person the owner named. You confirm by email first, and nothing is sent until you do.

BEACON never books a flight, holds an aircraft or takes payment. Any flight is arranged and operated by a certificated operator. No asking price is ever published.

Who it is for: shoppers in the US who want to check for a coupon code before they buy.

How it works: offers come from affiliate programs McClipFace has joined (CJ, Impact, Awin, Admitad, TakeDeals and direct brand programs) and from a licensed coupon data partner. Some returned links are affiliate links: if you buy after following one, McClipFace may earn a commission at no added cost to you, and every such link is disclosed. Commission never affects which offers are returned or how they are ranked. Links open only when you choose to shop through them.

Optional reporting: after you try a code, you can choose to report whether it worked. A report is sent only when you say yes to reporting that result, or if you turn on Community mode. Reports contain only the store, the code and the outcome, never cart contents, prices or personal data.

Limitations: coverage is limited to stores whose affiliate programs work with McClipFace, so many stores return no codes; that means McClipFace has no data for the store, not that no coupons exist. Codes are not guaranteed and the store's checkout has the final say. McClipFace does not sell products, make purchases or process payments. It never returns offers for stores selling adult products, tobacco, nicotine or vape products, CBD or THC, weapons, prescription drugs or other prohibited goods.

interface.short_description: Travel jobs and pay for nurses
interface.long_description:
Trusted Health helps travel nurses and allied clinicians find their next contract. This plugin gives you a live look at the Trusted marketplace inside ChatGPT, so you can ask the questions you'd ask a Trusted Advocate and get answers from current Trusted listings, without an account.

What you can ask:

- Find jobs. "Night L&D jobs in compact states starting before December." Search by role, specialty, state or city, shift, contract length, start date and minimum weekly pay.
- See how a job's pay compares. Each result shows estimated weekly pay, the total for the contract, and how the pay compares with the average for the same role in that state at the same weekly hours. When several jobs can be compared, the one furthest above average is flagged.
- Compare pay across states. "What do NICU travel nurses make in Texas compared with other states?" You get the average over the last 7 days, the range, the gap to the US average, and the states with the highest averages.
- Open the job on Trusted. Each card links to the full posting.

There's more on Trusted. The plugin is a live look. A Trusted account, where you confirm you're a real clinician, adds:
- Full pay breakdowns and facility details up front, before you apply.
- Real-time matches, ranked for you, the moment jobs post.
- A dedicated Advocate, as much or as little as you need.

Not looking right now? Set your status to "not looking" and still get daily matches and current rates. Know what you're worth, even if you're staying put.

Pay is Trusted's estimate of weekly gross pay: taxable pay plus tax-free stipends, before taxes, for all scheduled hours. Figures are rounded to the nearest $10 and come from the same data as the salary pages on trustedhealth.com.

Roles include registered nurses and LPN/LVNs, plus allied roles such as respiratory therapists, surgical technologists, physical and occupational therapists, sonographers, and lab and imaging technologists.

The plugin doesn't need an account and doesn't ask for personal, health or license information.

release.description: Audit a Meta Ads Manager CSV export for wasted spend, creative fatigue, below-break-even ad sets, budget-capped winners, under-delivery and rejected ads.

interface.short_description: Audit your Meta ads export
interface.long_description:
Ad Account Health Check reviews a Meta Ads Manager export and shows where spend is leaking.

What it checks: creative fatigue (click-through falling over the period), ad sets below your break-even ROAS, target CPA or target CPL, ad sets that perform well but are held back by their budget, under-delivering ad sets, and rejected ads. Each finding names the campaign, ad set or ad, explains why it was flagged, estimates the monthly impact where it can, and suggests a fix. You also get a 0-100 score and a list of the checks that could not run, with the reason.

How to export: in Meta Ads Manager open the Ads tab, set the date range to Last 30 days, choose Breakdown > By time > Day, then Reports > Export table data > CSV, and attach the file in ChatGPT. Ask "How do I export my Meta ads data?" for the full steps and the columns it uses.

How it works: the checks use the same deterministic rules engine and thresholds as Adcero's Optimize page, so the same file always gives the same result. Share your break-even ROAS, target CPA or target CPL to turn on the break-even checks.

What it can't check: it reads Meta exports only (not Google Ads, TikTok or other platforms); it needs an ad-level export broken down by day that covers at least 7 days; results are judged on Meta-reported purchases, which Meta's own attribution can over-count; and an export does not carry first-party store data, so new-customer cost checks are skipped.

Your account and data: it never connects to or changes your ad account; it only reads the file you share. The file itself is not stored. The derived report (score, findings and skipped checks) is kept for 14 days so you can open the full report from the link, then deleted unless you save it to an Adcero account. Privacy details: https://app.adcero.io/apps-privacy
capabilities: Audit a Meta Ads Manager CSV export (ad level, daily breakdown)
Flag creative fatigue, rejected ads and budget pacing problems
Run break-even ROAS, target CPA and target CPL checks when you provide them
Explain how to export the right report from Ads Manager

interface.long_description:
Kickaround puts your question to several AI models at once. They answer, read each other's answers and argue it out. Then Kickaround gives you one verdict: the best move, why, and what's still open.

Use it when one answer isn't enough: a job offer, a launch date, a big purchase, a plan you want torn apart, or a claim you want checked.

Choose how they work on it:
- Opine: a view or a decision (the default)
- Critique: poke holes in a plan or draft
- Research: check facts on the web, with sources
- Brainstorm: lots of ideas
- Summarize: the short version

Say "kickaround" with your question, for example "Kickaround whether I should take the job offer." A run takes a few minutes. The verdict comes back in the chat, with a link to the whole discussion on kickaround.app, where you can ask follow-ups.

You need a Kickaround account: sign in with Google when ChatGPT asks. Kickaround sees only the questions you send it, and your threads are private to you.

interface.short_description: Operate Bird from your agent

Connect Bird and Codex does all of it for real: email, SMS, and WhatsApp on Bird's own sending infrastructure and carrier connections, calls on Bird SIP trunks, live events to every open browser and app over Bird Realtime — with a delivery timestamp or the exact failure reason instead of a guess.

And Codex doesn't just send through Bird — it can own the endpoints. It claims its agent a durable email address in one call and answers what arrives there. Addresses, numbers, trunks, and the compliance behind them — acquired in conversation.

Whatever your account can do, Codex can do here. The tools are generated from Bird's live API — the same surface Bird's own dashboard runs on — so the list Codex shows is always the current one and grows as Bird does. Some of it works before you even connect: grade any domain's live email authentication, analyze headers and DMARC reports, or search Bird's docs, no account needed.

You sign in with Bird when you connect, so there is no API key to paste and no secret sitting in your config.toml. Codex gets only the permissions you already hold, and you can revoke them from your Bird profile.

A good first ask: "Send me a test email and tell me the moment it's delivered." Building an agent? "Claim yourself an email address and reply to whatever arrives."

What you can do:

Sign-in: when you connect, you enter the web address of your Perfex CRM and an API token created in Setup > API > API Management. ChatGPT gets exactly the permissions of that token, so you decide what it can see and change. Tools that delete records, overwrite fields or may email your customers are marked so that ChatGPT asks for your confirmation first.

Your data: the connector passes requests between ChatGPT and your CRM and does not store your CRM data. Your CRM address and token are kept encrypted only to keep you connected; disconnecting revokes access, and deleting the token in Perfex CRM stops it immediately.

Requirements: a self-hosted Perfex CRM reachable over https, with the REST API for Perfex CRM module by Themesic Interactive installed, licensed for that CRM's domain, and its MCP server enabled in Setup > API > Settings. Without the module the plugin cannot access your CRM.

Limitations: the plugin works only with the one CRM you connect, within the permissions of your token. It does not process card payments and cannot reach CRMs on private networks.

Perfex CRM is a trademark of its owner. This plugin is published by Themesic Interactive and is not affiliated with the makers of Perfex CRM.

release.description: Persistent memory for ChatGPT: remember facts and documents into your Cognee workspace, recall them with graph-aware search, and forget what you no longer need.

interface.short_description: Long-term memory for ChatGPT
interface.long_description:
Cognee gives ChatGPT a memory that lasts beyond one conversation. Everything you ask it to remember goes into your own Cognee Cloud workspace, where it is turned into a knowledge graph: entities, relationships and summaries, not just stored text. Later, in any conversation and from any client connected to the same workspace, ChatGPT can recall it with search that uses that structure, so answers draw on how facts connect rather than on keyword matches alone.

Four tools:
- remember: store text, or a file up to 10 MB, into a dataset. Cognee ingests it, extracts entities and relationships, and builds the graph.
- recall: search your memory with a natural-language question. Cognee routes it to the right retrieval strategy and returns an answer with the supporting memories, or the raw matching passages if you ask for them.
- forget: delete one item, one dataset, or everything you own.
- cognify_status: check on ingestion that was started in the background.

Memories are organised into datasets. By default ChatGPT writes to a dataset of its own, so what ChatGPT remembers stays separate from what your other tools remember, while recall searches across all of them. Name a dataset in the conversation to use a specific one.

You sign in with your Cognee account; no API key is pasted anywhere. Each call runs against your workspace with your own identity and permissions. Workspaces that have been idle go to sleep; the first call after a quiet period wakes one and can take about a minute.

Cognee is open source (github.com/topoteretes/cognee). This plugin is the hosted version of the Cognee MCP server, run by Cognee for Cognee Cloud workspaces. A Cognee Cloud account with a workspace is required.
capabilities: Remember facts and documents into a personal knowledge graph

release.description:
The Zuora MCP Server connects Zuora with large language models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT, through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). It enables AI-assisted analysis, reporting, and insights into your Zuora tenant data through conversational queries.

The Zuora MCP Server connects to your live Zuora data, SDKs, APIs, and supporting documentation sources, including the Developer Center and Zuora product documentation. Together, these sources give your team a unified view of Zuora as an Order-to-Revenue (OTR) platform.

The Zuora MCP Server supports the following teams by simplifying how they access and use Zuora data:

Financial analysis and reporting – Analyze key metrics, such as recurring revenue trends and subscription performance, by asking questions in natural language instead of manually building queries or reports.

Customer success – Retrieve account details, subscription status, and billing history without navigating multiple interfaces, so you can respond to customer inquiries faster.

skills.name: clause-comparator
skills.description: Compares the same clause or provision across draft rounds, precedents, public agreements or a portfolio and reports what differs in wording and effect. Use for version-change requests and external clause benchmarking, including "what changed between drafts", "compare their indemnity with ours", "compare liability caps across these SaaS agreements", "what indemnity approach is most common in public SaaS agreements", "what is typical", "what is prevalent" or "is this market standard". External frequency claims require a disclosed multi-document sample, not one precedent. Distinct from contract-reviewer, which grades an agreement for risk; this stays neutral unless a side is given. Fires for any clause type in any commercial agreement.

interface.short_description: Compare the same clause across drafts or a standard
interface.default_prompt: Use $clause-comparator to compare this clause across these drafts and report what actually changed.

skills.name: contract-drafter
skills.description: Drafts a complete contract from a term sheet, negotiated heads or plain instructions — parties, recitals, definitions, operative clauses, schedules and boilerplate — in a specified posture and matched to a supplied or requested precedent. Use for "draft a services agreement", "turn this term sheet into a contract", "prepare an NDA", "draft an SPA from our template", or requests to draft using public agreements, model forms or market examples. When external precedents are requested, it searches the plugin's listed contract sources before generic websites. Distinct from contract-reviewer, which analyses an existing agreement. Fires for any commercial agreement type.

interface.short_description: Draft agreements from a term sheet or instructions
interface.default_prompt: Use $contract-drafter to draft an agreement from this term sheet, in the specified drafting posture.

skills.name: contract-reviewer
skills.description: Reviews an entire draft or executed commercial contract, or an expressly scoped set of related provisions, from one identified party's perspective and produces ranked risks, exact clause citations and negotiation recommendations. Use for prompts such as "review this MSA from the Buyer's side", "what should we push back on across this agreement", "review only the IP and confidentiality provisions", or "conduct an exhaustive audit". Quick review is the default; focused and full-audit modes follow the user's scope. Do not use for a neutral summary, obligation extraction, version comparison, a single-clause rewrite, a focused liability or exit outcome question, or negotiation strategy.

interface.short_description: Rank contract risks from one identified party's side
interface.default_prompt: Use $contract-reviewer to review this agreement from the Buyer's side and rank the 10 most important legal and commercial risks.

skills.name: contract-summariser
skills.description: Produces a short, factual, neutral summary of what a contract actually does — the parties, what is being exchanged, the key commercial terms, and the handful of provisions worth knowing before reading the whole document. Use this when a user wants the gist rather than a review — including phrasings like "what does this contract actually say", "summarise this NDA for me", "give me the two-minute version of this agreement", "what are we actually signing up to", "plain-English rundown of this lease", or "brief the team on what this MSA covers". Neutral by default — it does not take a side or grade risk; hand off to contract-reviewer for that, or to obligations-extractor for a complete deadline ledger. Fires for any commercial agreement type.

interface.short_description: Plain, neutral summary of what an agreement does
interface.default_prompt: Use $contract-summariser to give me the plain-language gist of what this contract actually does.

skills.name: indemnity-liability-analyst
skills.description: Analyses the warranty, indemnity, exclusion, cap and insurance provisions in a contract as one interacting system for one identified party. Use for focused prompts such as "what is our exposure under this indemnity", "does the cap still protect the Supplier after the carve-outs", "which liabilities are capped or uncapped", or "does the IP indemnity sit inside the cap". Reports stated and functional caps, sub-caps, quantifiable exposure, apparently uncapped categories and unquantifiable dependencies. It does not infer insurance coverage without the actual policy. Distinct from contract-reviewer, which ranks issues across an agreement.

interface.short_description: Analyse liability caps, carve-outs, and insurance gaps
interface.default_prompt: Use $indemnity-liability-analyst to analyse the Supplier's exposure after applying the cap, carve-outs, and sub-caps.

skills.name: mou-drafter
skills.description: Drafts an MOU, letter of intent, heads of terms or term sheet from instructions, making the binding and non-binding parts explicit. Use for "draft an MOU for this joint venture", "prepare an LOI for the acquisition", "draft heads with binding exclusivity", "turn these terms into an MOU", or requests to draft using public MOUs, model forms or comparable provisions. When external precedents are requested, it searches the plugin's listed contract sources before generic websites. Distinct from contract-drafter, which produces a definitive agreement.

interface.short_description: Draft MOUs with binding parts made explicit
interface.default_prompt: Use $mou-drafter to draft an MOU for this deal, making clear exactly which parts are binding.

skills.name: negotiation-position-planner
skills.description: Builds an opening position, fallback, minimum acceptable position, walk-away line and concession logic for contract negotiations. When external benchmarks are requested, it searches the plugin's listed contract sources before generic websites. For several issues, it also covers priority, sequencing, trades and dependencies. Distinct from redline-proposer and contract-reviewer.

interface.short_description: Plan opening, fallback, and walk-away positions
interface.default_prompt: Use $negotiation-position-planner to plan our opening, fallback, minimum acceptable, and walk-away positions on this open point.

skills.name: obligations-extractor
skills.description: Pulls every obligation, deadline, condition and notice requirement out of a contract into a structured ledger, without evaluating whether any of it is fair, onerous or negotiable. Use this whenever a user wants a list, table or calendar of what a contract actually requires — including phrasings like "list every obligation in this agreement", "what are our deadlines under this contract", "build a compliance calendar from this MSA", "pull out everything we have to deliver and by when", "extract the notice periods", "what do we owe them and what do they owe us", or "turn this contract into a checklist". Use for "redline this liability clause", "give me alternatives for this indemnity", "rewrite this termination clause", "propose language for clause 9", or requests for wording based on public clauses, model forms or market examples. When external wording is requested, it searches the plugin's listed contract sources before generic websites. Distinct from contract-reviewer and negotiation-position-planner. Fires for any clause type in any commercial agreement.

interface.short_description: Draft alternative wording from aggressive to fallback
interface.default_prompt: Use $redline-proposer to rewrite this clause with strongest credible, balanced, and minimum acceptable versions.

skills.name: termination-analyst
skills.description: Reads every termination, notice, cure and survival clause in a contract as one system, for one identified party, and reports how each party can actually get out, on what notice, and what happens next — including whether a client's live intent to terminate right now would actually satisfy the trigger as drafted. Use this whenever a user wants the exit position worked through in depth rather than as one part of a full review — including phrasings like "can we terminate this for breach", "what notice do we need to give to get out of this MSA", "does this failure count as a material breach under the contract", "what survives if we terminate", "is our termination right weaker than theirs", or "can they walk away from this with no notice at all". interface.default_prompt: Use $termination-analyst to work out how each party can actually get out of this contract, and what survives.

Use this whenever a user is preparing a submission for a mediator — including phrasings like "draft our mediation brief", "prepare a confidential brief for the mediator", "write a brief we're sharing with the other side too", or "set out our position and interests for this mediation". skills.name: mediation-opening-drafter
skills.description: Drafts the opening statement delivered at the start of a joint mediation session — calibrated for a spoken, in-person audience that includes the other party, protecting the bottom line and any weaknesses, and flagging any line that signals more flexibility or more hostility than the client actually authorised. Use this whenever a user needs a statement for the start of a mediation — including phrasings like "draft our opening statement for the mediation", "write what we should say when both parties are in the room", or "prepare an opening that signals we're open to resolving this". Distinct from mediation-brief-drafter, which is a written submission to the mediator — this is spoken, delivered face to face with the other party present. Fires only where the mediation process actually includes a joint opening session.

interface.short_description: Draft spoken opening statements for a joint session
interface.default_prompt: Use $mediation-opening-drafter to draft our opening statement for the mediation.

skills.name: mediation-outcome-documenter
skills.description: Records what was actually agreed in a mediation session and what remains open — distinguishing full agreement from agreement-in-principle, noting every condition attached, and never treating the record itself as the binding settlement document unless the user confirms that is what's intended. Use this whenever a user needs a session documented — including phrasings like "record what we agreed today", "document the outcome of this mediation session", "write up what's settled and what's still open", or "capture the next steps from today's session". Distinct from settlement-terms-drafter, which converts a completed settlement into full binding terms — this documents what actually happened in the room. Fires after any mediation session, whether it ended in full settlement, partial agreement, or no agreement.

interface.short_description: Record what a mediation session actually agreed
interface.default_prompt: Use $mediation-outcome-documenter to record what we agreed today, and what remains open.

skills.name: party-interest-analyst
skills.description: Separates each party's stated position from their actual underlying interests, for both sides of a dispute, tagging every interest as confirmed from direct instruction or inferred from conduct — and maps where positions conflict but interests might not, without pretending every conflict has a win-win answer. Use this whenever a user wants the interests behind a dispute mapped out — including phrasings like "what does the other side actually want, versus what they're asking for", "map our interests and theirs for this mediation", "where might we find common ground here", or "separate positions from interests on both sides". Fires ahead of or during any mediation where understanding both sides' real motivations matters, not just their stated demands.

interface.short_description: Separate stated positions from underlying interests
interface.default_prompt: Use $party-interest-analyst to map both parties' positions and their underlying interests.

skills.name: settlement-evaluator
skills.description: Tests a specific settlement offer against the realistic alternative of continuing to litigate — an expected-value comparison with the arithmetic shown, layered with what pure expected value misses — certainty, the client's actual risk tolerance, and hidden costs in the offer's own conditions. Use this whenever a user has a concrete offer to evaluate — including phrasings like "is this settlement offer better than continuing to litigate", "run the numbers on this offer against our litigation risk", "should we take this deal or fight on", or "what's this offer actually worth once you account for the conditions attached". Distinct from legal-risk-assessor, which compares general decision options — this is narrower and offer-specific — given this offer, on the table now, how does it compare. Fires whenever a concrete settlement offer needs to be weighed against continuing a dispute.

interface.short_description: Test an offer against the litigation alternative
interface.default_prompt: Use $settlement-evaluator to test this settlement offer against our realistic litigation alternative.

interface.short_description: Legal research workflows
